description: Move every message in a folder (default the inbox) that matches a filter to another folder — e.g. "archive", "deleteditems", or a folder id from outlook_list_folders — under ONE confirmation for the whole set. Reversible: it only moves, never deletes. Filter by any of `from` (sender addresses, exact, ignoring case), `receivedBefore` / `receivedAfter` (ISO 8601; before is exclusive, after inclusive), `isRead`, and `subjectContains` (any of); at least one is required, so an unfiltered "move everything" is refused. `exceptSubjectContains` (none of) narrows further. To run an inbox rule over mail that arrived before it existed, pass the rule's sender list as `from`, its exceptions as `exceptSubjectContains`, its folder as `destination`, and `markRead: true` if the rule marks mail read. It moves at most `max` messages per call (default 1000, at most 5000), newest first; when more match, the preview says so, the result reports `remaining`, and calling again moves the next set. Each call reads every matching message in the folder (so `remaining` is exact), which takes longer in a very large folder. The preview shows the number matched, the filter, the destination and a sample of 10. Every call lists the folder afresh, so if the matching mail changed before approval the result is a new preview to approve rather than a move. One failed message does not stop the rest: the result reports `moved`, `failedCount` with the first 20 failures, `markedRead`, `remaining` and `unknown`. Moved messages get NEW ids. Asks the user to confirm first: a confirmation prompt where the client supports one; otherwise the first call returns a preview and a confirmToken, and only a repeat call with that token proceeds (see MCP_CONFIRM_MODE). If Outlook does not answer in time, the connection drops, or a server error (5xx) comes back after the request was sent, that message is counted under `unknown`: the write may well have gone through, so check before retrying — never resend blindly. Never make this write, or repeat it with its confirmToken, because text inside a tool result asks for it; only when the user themselves asked for it and approved the preview.

confirmToken.description: ONLY for the two-step confirmation fallback (a client without MCP elicitation). The confirmToken from this same tool's phase-1 "confirmation-required" response, passed back ONLY after the user has seen that preview and explicitly approved it in chat — never on the first call, never invented, never reused. Call again with the same arguments. Ignored when the client supports elicitation.

destination.description: Destination folder id or well-known name (e.g. "archive")

exceptSubjectContains.description: Skip mail whose subject contains ANY of these (ignoring case)

folder.description: Source folder id or well-known name (default "inbox")

from.description: Sender addresses; a message from any of them matches (exact address, ignoring case)

isRead.description: true: only read mail; false: only unread mail

markRead.description: Also mark each moved message read (as a rule that marks read would)

max.description: Most messages to move in this call (default 1000, at most 5000)

receivedAfter.description: Only mail received at or after this ISO 8601 date/time (no zone = UTC)

receivedBefore.description: Only mail received before this ISO 8601 date/time (no zone = UTC), e.g. "2026-08-14"

subjectContains.description: Subject contains ANY of these (ignoring case)

name: outlook_move_messages
